question: Should companies be required to make their products repairable, even if that makes them more expensive to buy?
Should cities give more road space to public transport, even if that leaves less room for private cars?
Should employers provide paid time for staff to learn new skills, even if that reduces the time spent on their usual work?
Should everyone receive a basic income, even if funding it requires higher income taxes?
Should school meals be free for every child, even if that leaves less funding for other school services?
Should governments tax foods high in added sugar, even if that makes some everyday groceries more expensive?
Should universities be free to attend, with the cost shared by taxpayers who may never attend one?
Should large employers reserve half their board seats for women, even if that limits their choice of candidates?
Should households pay a higher rate for water used above a basic allowance, even in places where water is currently plentiful?
Should communities be able to block nearby wind farms, even if that delays national clean-energy targets?
Should publicly funded inventions be free for any company to use, even if that reduces the income available for further research?
Should large inheritances be taxed more heavily than income earned through work?
Should people who fly frequently pay higher taxes on each additional flight they take in a year?
Should commercial fishing be banned in some marine areas, even if nearby fishing communities lose income?
Should governments pay farmers to restore wildlife habitats on productive farmland, even if that reduces domestic food production?
Should public officials publish records of their meetings with lobbyists, even if that makes some organisations less willing to speak openly?
Should governments maintain overseas aid spending during a domestic recession, even when public services at home face cuts?
Should financial support be available to everyone below an income threshold without a requirement to look for work?
Should governments prioritise locally grown food for public institutions, even when imported food costs less?
Should health services move more funding into preventing illness, even if that leaves less money for treatments available today?
Should schools give practical life skills the same teaching time as academic subjects, even if pupils cover less academic material?
Should each parent have an equal share of paid parental leave that cannot be transferred to the other parent?
Should new housing be delayed in areas with limited water supplies, even when those areas urgently need more homes?
Should governments fund new nuclear power stations, even though they create radioactive waste that needs long-term management?
Should workers have a legal right to predictable weekly hours, even if employers respond by offering fewer jobs?
Should governments prioritise reliable internet in remote communities over faster connections in cities, even if it costs more per household?
Should employers favour applicants from disadvantaged backgrounds when candidates are equally qualified?
Should cities allow taller apartment buildings in existing neighbourhoods, even when residents want to preserve the area's character?
Should shops be prohibited from destroying unsold goods, even if storing, donating or recycling them increases business costs?
Should wealthier countries cut emissions faster than poorer countries, even if that raises their costs of doing business?
